audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Katarina/Skill/Skill while the content layer and the packet both read Viktor/Viktor/Viktor/Viktor/Katarina/Katarina/Viktor. The page renders two different answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: Viktor's Siphon Power (Q, 9/8/7/6/5s) shields the trade and empowers an auto, and Hextech Ray (E, 12/11/10/9/8s) pokes through the wave at 525 range; Katarina has no ranged answer until Death Lotus at 6. Content whys are grounded and match the packet, so the full layer is the wrong copy.
audit.corrected: Move phases[0..3].side to Viktor, phases[5].side to Katarina, phases[6].side to Viktor, ratings adjusted, whys rewritten to match. Content win[] already holds the correct verdicts.

audit.why: spikes[] already name Lvl 6 as the flip, first item as the extension window, and late as Viktor's via full Hexcore augments. Level 6 Death Lotus vs Arcane Storm (120/100/80s) is the real spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction — Gravity Field (W) stunning you out of a channelling Death Lotus, and Arcane Storm itself interrupting channels — is never stated as a cancel. breakdown.cooldowns carries no cooldown number at all.
audit.why: Katarina's R is flagged channel: interruptible — any CC cancels it. Viktor's W is hardCC and his R text explicitly says it interrupts enemy channels. Both cancel your ultimate.
audit.corrected: State that Gravity Field (17/16/15/14/13s) and Arcane Storm both end Death Lotus, and give the real numbers in breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns; the kit gives Gravity Field 17/16/15/14/13, Hextech Ray 12/11/10/9/8, Shunpo 12/11/10/9/8, Death Lotus 75/60/45.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d is the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d is the tradeBad string verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED). dontsFull[2].t also references spell-shield kits, which Viktor does not have.
audit.why: Title promises one thing and the body explains another; Viktor has no spell shield anywhere in his kit.
audit.corrected: Both bullets rewritten to their own titles, and the spell-shield title replaced with Viktor's actual shield source.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Katarina

edits.before: Q the wave and collect the dagger — every pickup is a free spin; the lane learns your dagger geometry or bleeds.
edits.after: Siphon Power shields his side of every exchange and empowers the auto, so your Q bounce loses the trade — take the dagger, not the fight.

edits.before: W joins: drop, dance, collect — the self-dagger speeds your trades and your exits both.
edits.after: Hextech Ray lands at 2 and cuts through the wave while he last-hits; W only buys you the speed to leave the line, not to win it.

edits.before: Full kit: E to daggers, not faces — the blink economy is the champion; trade only through steel on the ground.
edits.after: His Q-into-E cycle plus a pre-dropped Gravity Field denies clean Shunpo angles — blink to daggers behind the wave and keep the HP bar.

edits.before: Dagger-trade on cooldown: Q-E-W-E strings chunk and the resets... wait for kills. Bank the patterns.
edits.after: He holds you under all-in HP with an 8-second Hextech Ray while Siphon Power erases what you chip back. Bank patterns; do not commit.

edits.before: First item spike: full dagger strings delete squishies and one kill opens the chain reaction.
edits.after: First item keeps the 6-11 window open — your spike is live while he is still buying Hex Fragments, so punish every E spent on the wave.

edits.before: Late Kata is a chain reaction: enter on daggers, lotus the clump, reset through the wreckage, repeat until silence.
edits.after: Augmented Hextech Ray adds an explosion behind the line and Arcane Storm interrupts channels outright — front-door entries die, so pick him in fog first.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. It governs your forward steps. - E Shunpo (second use) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Gravity Field is 17s at rank 1, 13s maxed, and it stuns you out of a channelling Death Lotus — that one button is the matchup. - Hextech Ray is 12s at rank 1; when he throws it at the wave you have your window. - Shunpo is 12s early: spend it on poke and your 75-second Death Lotus has no entry.

edits.before: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — steel-routed trades his aim can't follow.
edits.after: Walk him into throwing Gravity Field on empty air, then count 13-17 seconds — inside that window Death Lotus finishes without an interrupt.

edits.before: All-in into spell-shield kits unbroken
edits.after: All-in into a fresh Siphon Power shield

edits.before: Shunpo onto a face with the CC still loaded — Katarina dies to held buttons, not skill, and everyone holding one knows it.
edits.after: His Q shield lands the instant you commit and eats the front of your string; open after he has spent it on the wave, not before.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Viktor wins by stunning your Death Lotus mid-channel with Gravity Field, then scaling to augmented Hextech Ray that chunks you before you enter.

edits.before: Ahead, chain it: zone Viktor off daggers, lotus every skirmish, and reset through the map — fed Katarina is a weather event.
edits.after: Ahead, deny Hex Fragments: he needs 100 per augment, so every kill you take off him delays the late game that beats you. Roam — he cannot follow.

edits.before: Carry through chain reactions — one kill is three; your job is the first domino and the discipline to wait for it.
edits.after: Carry by ending it inside 6-11, before his Hexcore fills. Every reset you take is an augment he never buys — that is the whole clock.

edits.before: If Viktor gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Gravity Field extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q bounces and stay relevant through reset potential.
edits.after: A kill for Viktor is 100 Hex Fragments closer to an augment, so it compounds twice. Farm out of Hextech Ray's 525-range line, take the safe Q bounce, and wait for a jungle setup instead of forcing.

edits.before: Level 2 Death Ray poke through the wave chunks you faster than you can answer.
edits.after: Level 2 Hextech Ray poke through the wave chunks you faster than you can answer.

edits.before: At 6 Death Lotus point-blank beats early Chaos Storm and out-races W's 0.75s arm time.
edits.after: At 6 Death Lotus point-blank beats a rank-1 Arcane Storm on its 120-second cooldown.

edits.before: Still his lane: Siphon Power shields his trades, Gravity Field zones your Shunpo angles, and Death Ray farms while poking you. Take short Q-bounce pokes only, keep 60%+ HP, and stack CS — your window is coming at 6, not here.
edits.after: Still his lane: Siphon Power shields his trades, Gravity Field zones your Shunpo angles, and Hextech Ray farms while poking you. Take short Q-bounce pokes only, keep 60%+ HP, and stack CS — your window is coming at 6, not here.

edits.before: Your Lvl 6-11 window stays open through first item: he's still gathering Hexcore upgrades while you have a real spike. Punish every Death Ray he uses on the wave with a full-combo trade.
edits.after: Your Lvl 6-11 window stays open through first item: he needs 100 Hex Fragments per augment while you already have a real spike. Punish every Hextech Ray he spends on the wave with a full-combo trade.

edits.before: Fully upgraded Viktor out-teamfights you — augmented E chunks half your HP at screen range and W+R melts your Lotus. You need flanks and picks before fights start, not front-door entries.
edits.after: Fully upgraded Viktor out-teamfights you — augmented Hextech Ray adds an explosion behind the line, and Gravity Field or Arcane Storm ends your Lotus mid-channel. You need flanks and picks before fights start, not front-door entries.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 respect him: Siphon Power gives him a shield plus an empowered auto every short trade, and Death Ray at 2 chunks you through the wave while last-hitting. Your Bouncing Blade poke loses the exchange when his Q shield eats half of it. Take farm with Q bounces from max range, sacrifice a few CS to skillshots rather than your health bar, and let him push — a frozen or slow-pushing wave near your tower is where you eventually kill him.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 respect him: Siphon Power gives him a shield plus an empowered auto every short trade, and Hextech Ray at 2 chunks you through the wave while last-hitting. Your Q bounce loses the exchange into a fresh Q shield, and his Q is only 9 seconds at rank 1. Take farm from the 625-range Q, sacrifice a few CS to skillshots rather than your health bar, and let him push — a frozen or slow-pushing wave near your tower is where you eventually kill him.

edits.before: Poke you sub-60% with E so your all-in maths never works
edits.after: Poke you sub-60% with Hextech Ray so your all-in maths never works

edits.before: Drop Gravity Field on his own feet the moment you commit Death Lotus
edits.after: Stun your Death Lotus mid-channel with Gravity Field dropped on his own feet

notes: Full-layer level chart disagreed with content win[] on six of seven rows (full said Skill, content and packet said Viktor/Katarina). All six side edits proposed as one atomic group with their whys and ratings; no paired win[N] edits were needed because the content layer already holds the target values — the disagreement was one-sided. Ability-name errors from the packet confirmed against the kit: 'Death Ray' is Hextech Ray (E), 'Chaos Storm' is Arcane Storm (R); both fixed everywhere they appear in writable prose. 'Bouncing Blade' is not in Riot's text for Katarina's Q — the kit gives no name for that slot, so I replaced the phrase with the mechanic and the 625 range rather than assert a name. Left alone and unverified: the 0.75s Gravity Field arm time cited in spikes[1].text, breakdown.mid and late — the kit carries no cast/arm timing, so I could not confirm or correct it; those two remaining mentions still contain it. Also unverified: whether Cleanse or tenacity shortens the Gravity Field stun enough to save a Death Lotus. report[] left untouched apart from nothing — no report entry named a fabricated ability that the lint flagged. | COHERENCE: 5 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
